note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypertension and palpitations.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
49-year-old male with long-standing history of hypertension since young age. Recently presented to emergency room in March with elevated blood pressure and palpitations. Patient attributes this episode to consuming several cups of coffee without breakfast, possibly representing a panic attack. Denies recurrence of palpitations since that time. States blood pressure has been improving since starting new medication approximately one month ago prescribed by new primary care doctor. Currently monitoring blood pressure at home daily in the morning, with readings ranging from 146-155 mmHg. Patient reports attempting to reduce salt intake and exercises on treadmill when able.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No palpitations since March emergency room visit. Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or other concerning symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension since young age.

MEDICATIONS
Benicar HCT (olmesartan 40-25 mg, containing hydrochlorothiazide) - started approximately one month ago.
Amlodipine 10 mg daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Significant for hypertension in multiple family members.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Exercises on treadmill when able. Attempting to reduce salt intake.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Heart and lungs: Clear to auscultation, sounds good.
Abdomen: No tenderness to palpation.
Extremities: No edema noted in ankles and feet.

RESULTS
Potassium one week ago: 4.0 (normal).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
49-year-old male with resistant hypertension on three medications at maximum doses with blood pressure still not at goal (146-155 mmHg). Plan to add spironolactone to medication regimen. Patient counseled on potential side effects including possible dizziness, gynecomastia (rare), and electrolyte disturbances including hyperkalemia and hyponatremia. Emphasized importance of hydration. Scheduled for follow-up in two weeks with metabolic panel and blood pressure check to monitor potassium and sodium levels. Patient counseled on importance of blood pressure control to prevent complications including left ventricular hypertrophy, heart failure, stroke, and kidney failure. Provided information on DASH eating plan, American Heart Association resources, and benefits of regular aerobic exercise. If inadequate response to spironolactone, will consider referral to resistant hypertension clinic for evaluation of secondary causes and consideration of procedure-based interventions such as renal denervation.
